question.text: The reaction of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Xe</mi><mrow/></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> gives a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Xe</mi></math> compound <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math>. The number of moles of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>HF</mi></math> produced by the complete hydrolysis of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math> is _____ .

solution.text:
Xe+2O2 F2→XeF4P+2O2

6XeF4P+12H2O⟶4Xe+2XeO3+24HF+3O2

Number of moles of HF formed by complete hydrolysis of 1 mole of P=4
